question: Why do researchers use the exact same questions and words for everyone taking a survey?

options.A: It prevents participants from feeling confused by long medical terms
options.B: It guarantees that every participant will finish the survey faster
options.C: It allows the nurse researcher to change the topic mid-interview
options.D: It ensures all answers can be fairly compared across the group

explanation: Using identical wording means any differences in the responses are due to actual differences between people, not because a question was asked differently. Keep pushing forward!

question: According to the World Health Organization, true health is much more than just not being sick. What else does it include?

options.A: It includes complete physical, mental, and social well-being
options.B: It requires regular laboratory blood test monitoring
options.C: It focuses primarily on the absence of chronic illness
options.D: It measures physical endurance and athletic capacity

explanation: Think about it like this: a person might be free from disease, but if they are stressed mentally or struggling socially, they aren't fully healthy yet. Health is the whole package!

question: Why do health workers treat gender-based violence as a major public health emergency?

options.A: It only affects women living in rural environments
options.B: It primarily places financial strain on hospital pharmacies
options.C: It causes widespread physical and psychological harm across communities
options.D: It is classified as a rare infectious disease outbreak

explanation: You got it! Because it hurts so many people physically and emotionally, healthcare systems treat it as a top priority to keep communities safe.

question: What type of mask must nurses wear when walking into an active TB patient's room?

options.A: Standard paper surgical mask for fluid splashes
options.B: Particulate respirator such as an N95 mask
options.C: Cloth face covering made from thick cotton fabric
options.D: Plastic face shield with no respiratory filter

explanation: Because TB travels on tiny air particles, ordinary surgical masks won't cut it. An N95 respirator keeps healthcare workers safe!

question: What is the most important assessment when checking a limb's circulation and nerve function after a joint procedure?

options.A: Measuring the exact circumference of the thigh
options.B: Listening for bowel sounds in the lower abdomen
options.C: Checking the patient's oral temperature reading
options.D: Checking pulse, color, movement, and sensation

explanation: Neurovascular checks (the famous '5 Ps' or pulse, color, movement, and sensation) help you catch any blood flow or nerve issues early before they turn into major complications.

question: Which of these is a major activity of voluntary health agencies?

options.A: Passing national laws in the legislative assembly
options.B: Conducting health education and disease prevention
options.C: Arresting individuals who violate public sanitary codes
options.D: Setting official salaries for government doctors

explanation: Correct! Voluntary agencies love teaching people simple hygiene and wellness habits to stop diseases before they start.

question: When helping a patient move from a bed to a chair, which direction should they generally pivot?

options.A: Toward the side with the IV pole
options.B: Toward the patient's stronger side
options.C: Toward the nurse's dominant hand
options.D: Toward the wall for extra privacy

explanation: Guiding them toward their stronger side lets them use their own strength and keeps them feeling secure during the turn.

question: Which severe obstetric complication is frequently linked to early childbearing before the pelvis is fully developed?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.B: Gestational diabetes
options.C: Obstetric fistula
options.D: Chronic hypertension

explanation: Prolonged and obstructed labor in an immature pelvis creates abnormal holes between the birth canal and bladder or rectum, leading to continuous leakage. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h3)

question: How can bedside nurses directly help with hospital financial efficiency?

options.A: By collecting taxes from patients at the hospital gate
options.B: By preventing waste of medical supplies and reducing patient complications
options.C: By negotiating insurance premium rates directly with corporate bosses
options.D: By deciding the annual national health budget in Parliament

explanation: As a nurse, being careful with consumables and preventing infections (like bedsores) means patients heal faster and use fewer resources—saving everyone money!

question: What is the main difference between parenteral (injectable) and oral anticoagulants?

options.A: Parenteral agents are injected for fast action, while oral agents are swallowed for long-term use
options.B: Parenteral drugs only target platelets, while oral drugs target the whole clotting cascade
options.C: Oral medications are only used in emergency intensive care units
options.D: Oral agents never require lab tests, whereas parenteral drugs need daily blood checks

explanation: You got it! When we need a fast response in an emergency, we inject it (parenteral). For long-term home use, pills (oral) are much easier for patients.

question: What is the most immediate life-threatening complication that can occur during the third stage of labor?

options.A: Neonatal jaundice
options.B: Postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Postpartum depression

explanation: Excessive bleeding after delivery can lead to hypovolemic shock and maternal death within a very short time if not managed urgently. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h4)

question: Why do many teenagers suddenly struggle with acne and body odor during puberty?

options.A: Increased hormone activity stimulates sweat and oil glands
options.B: Dietary habits change completely during the teenage years
options.C: The lymphatic system becomes temporarily blocked by growth
options.D: Skin cells stop shedding their outer protective layers

explanation: Spot on! Surging hormones wake up our sebaceous (oil) and sweat glands, leading to extra oil and body odor. Totally normal part of growing up!

question: Why is physical therapy for a stroke survivor considered tertiary prevention?

options.A: It limits disability and helps restore function after the damage has happened
options.B: It screens the general population for hidden high blood pressure
options.C: It stops the stroke from occurring in a healthy person
options.D: It eliminates environmental toxins that cause blood vessel disease

explanation: Exactly! Rehabilitation is all about helping patients regain independence and manage existing health challenges.

question: Why is it so important to treat strep throat quickly with antibiotics?

options.A: To ensure the patient never catches another cold ever again
options.B: To permanently shrink the size of the palatine tonsils
options.C: To cure viral rhinitis and clear nasal congestion instantly
options.D: To prevent serious systemic complications like rheumatic fever

explanation: Spot on! Early treatment stops strep bacteria from travelling around the body and causing serious issues like rheumatic heart disease.

question: Why must a nurse sort and classify healthcare waste right at the bedside?

options.A: It prevents hazardous items from mixing with safe trash and reducing risks.
options.B: It makes the waste room look neat and tidy for incoming visitors.
options.C: It ensures that kitchen scraps are safely sterilized before recycling.
options.D: It helps the hospital save money on buying heavy-duty office paper.

explanation: Spot on! Sorting waste right away stops dangerous things like used needles from ending up in normal trash bags where they could easily prick and injure anyone handling them.

question: How should the weights attached to Gallows traction hang?

options.A: Hanging freely without touching the floor or bed
options.B: Resting gently on the edge of the mattress
options.C: Adjusted by parents every few hours
options.D: Touching the floor for stability

explanation: Weights need to swing completely free in the air to give the exact pulling force required. If they touch the floor, the weight is off!

question: Why can a brain abscess cause symptoms that look just like a brain tumor?

options.A: It acts as a mass that takes up space and increases pressure inside the skull.
options.B: It causes the hair on the scalp to fall out rapidly.
options.C: It replaces normal brain cells with cancer cells.
options.D: It changes the genetic makeup of surrounding neurons over time.

explanation: A pocket of pus inside the head takes up physical space, just like a tumor. This raises the pressure inside the skull (ICP) and presses on nearby brain areas.

question: A nurse manager assigns an unverified temporary nurse to a fragile patient without checking references, and the patient gets hurt. What legal issue pops up?

options.A: Automatic suspension of the hospital's corporate tax license
options.B: Vicarious liability shifting entirely away from the hospital entity
options.C: Negligent credentialing and direct administrative liability for the manager
options.D: Total exemption of the temporary nurse from personal legal penalties

explanation: Skipping background checks and putting unqualified people on the floor lands straight on the manager and the facility as negligent credentialing.

question: Why is it important to regularly check the connection joints of an IV setup?

options.A: To ensure the gravity roller clamp is set to the maximum speed
options.B: To check if the plastic tubing needs to be warmed with a heating pad
options.C: To make sure the manufacturer label matches the client's chart
options.D: To prevent accidental disconnection, fluid leakage, and bacterial entry

explanation: Keeping connections tight keeps the system sterile! It stops messy leaks and prevents nasty bacteria from sneaking into your patient's bloodstream.

question: Why is proper nutrition considered a core element of Primary Health Care?

options.A: Nutrition is only important for professional athletes
options.B: Good nutrition strengthens immunity and prevents infectious diseases
options.C: Eating expensive foreign food cures chronic illnesses
options.D: Food supply is managed strictly by the federal military

explanation: Well-nourished bodies fight off infections much more effectively, reducing the burden of disease in the community. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h3)

question: How does General Paralysis of the Insane (GPI) usually show up in a patient?

options.A: It strikes suddenly right after a head injury.
options.B: It appears a few days after a bad cough or cold.
options.C: It is passed down directly from parents to children in their genes.
options.D: It develops many years after an untreated syphilis infection.

explanation: Spot on! GPI is a late complication of neurosyphilis that quietly creeps in years or even decades after the initial infection was missed or left untreated.

question: What is the main goal of bimanual palpation during a female pelvic exam?

options.A: To check for external skin lesions on the labia majora
options.B: To collect a sample of surface cells from the outer surface of the cervix
options.C: To measure the exact pH balance of vaginal fluid secretions
options.D: To evaluate the size, shape, and consistency of internal organs like the uterus

explanation: Spot on! By placing one hand inside the vagina and the other on the lower belly, you can 'sandwich' the organs to feel their size and tenderness.

question: Why is keeping the 'cold chain' so important when handling vaccines?

options.A: To make the injection feel more comfortable for the patient
options.B: To prevent the growth of harmful bacteria inside the glass vial
options.C: To ensure the chemical potency and effectiveness of the vaccine
options.D: To extend the manufacturer expiration date by several years

explanation: Brilliant! Heat can easily ruin the active ingredients in vaccines, rendering them useless if the cold chain breaks.

question: Who is most likely to require custodial care over a long period?

options.A: An athlete recovering from a simple sports-related ankle sprain
options.B: A patient with a sudden bacterial infection needing a short antibiotic course
options.C: A person admitted to the emergency ward with acute appendicitis
options.D: An individual with chronic physical disabilities or severe cognitive loss

explanation: People with chronic disabilities or long-term cognitive decline often lose the ability to care for themselves independently, making custodial support necessary. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of adding PEEP (positive end-expiratory pressure) to a ventilator?

options.A: To keep tiny air sacs in the lungs from collapsing at the end of exhalation
options.B: To force carbon dioxide out of the bloodstream into the lungs faster
options.C: To prevent the patient from waking up during sedation holidays
options.D: To measure the exact strength of the patient's heart contractions

explanation: PEEP acts like a gentle push that keeps the tiny lung air sacs open, making it much easier for the patient to absorb oxygen.

question: What is a great nursing strategy to help a patient manage a confusing medication schedule?

options.A: Asking the doctor to change frequent daily doses to a once-daily option
options.B: Instructing the patient to double up doses whenever they feel tired
options.C: Removing reminder alarms so the patient learns independence
options.D: Writing instructions in complex medical terminology for clarity

explanation: Simpler is always better! Cutting down how many times a day a patient must take a pill makes it much easier to remember.

question: How do you properly start a 24-hour urine collection test for a patient?

options.A: Save all urine produced starting from midnight regardless of when the patient last urinated
options.B: Collect the very first morning urine sample and use that exact time to start the 24-hour clock
options.C: Wait until the patient drinks two liters of water before collecting the first sample
options.D: Have the patient empty their bladder completely, discard that urine, and start the timer

explanation: Always throw away that very first void to empty the bladder completely, then start your 24-hour clock with a clean slate!

question: In research language, what do we mean by the term 'population'?

options.A: The nurses working in a specific hospital ward
options.B: Only the patients who agree to sign the consent form
options.C: The entire group of people the researcher wants to study
options.D: A small group of animals used in laboratory testing

explanation: Correct! The 'population' is the big picture—the complete group of people you are curious about and want your findings to apply to.

question: What is a false social norm regarding adolescent sexual activity?

options.A: Believing that parents support early teenage marriage
options.B: Believing that all or most peers are sexually active when many are not
options.C: Thinking that schools provide too much health education
options.D: Assuming that condoms are effective at preventing all diseases

explanation: Teens frequently overestimate how many of their peers are having sex because of boasting, which makes them feel abnormal if they remain abstinent. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h4)

question: Why should outbreak control measures sometimes start before lab results are fully finalized?

options.A: To avoid paperwork and administrative meetings
options.B: Because laboratory tests are always completely inaccurate
options.C: Because doctors are not allowed to read lab reports
options.D: To prevent further spread and save lives immediately

explanation: Waiting for lab work during a fast-moving crisis can cost lives. Taking action early based on clinical signs is a lifesaver!

question: Why does the nervous system use electrical impulses for communication?

options.A: To store long-term memories in the blood
options.B: To provide rapid and specific responses to body changes
options.C: To produce hormones for the digestive tract
options.D: To filter waste products out of the brain

explanation: Electrical impulses allow the body to react almost immediately to internal and external stimuli, which is essential for survival. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why are healthy adults able to hold their urine even when their bladder feels quite full?

options.A: The external sphincter fuses shut until voluntary pressure is applied.
options.B: Sympathetic tone permanently paralyzes the detrusor muscle.
options.C: Higher brain centers send inhibitory signals that prevent the micturition reflex from executing.
options.D: The kidneys temporarily stop producing urine until a bathroom is found.

explanation: Your brain's higher centers have great self-control! They send downward messages to hold off the reflex until you actually reach a restroom.

question: What is the main sign of the bargaining stage?

options.A: Directing intense rage at doctors and family members
options.B: Completely accepting the diagnosis without any sorrow
options.C: Isolating oneself from all hospital staff and visitors
options.D: Attempting to negotiate for more time or less pain

explanation: In this stage, patients try to make a 'deal'—often with God or fate—to buy a little more time.

question: Why do healthcare professionals classify traditional practices like female genital mutilation as public health issues rather than private matters?

options.A: They are strictly required by national constitutions
options.B: They cause widespread physical and psychological harm
options.C: They cost hospitals too much money to treat
options.D: They are exclusively performed inside public clinics

explanation: Any practice that inflicts severe, widespread bodily and mental injury on a population falls squarely under public health concern. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h1)

question: What is the main role of multimodal sensory association areas?

options.A: To store permanent language dictionaries in the brainstem
options.B: To combine inputs from multiple senses into a single experience
options.C: To send initial motor commands directly to skeletal muscles
options.D: To generate raw electrical impulses in the sensory organs

explanation: Multimodal areas act like a mixing desk, taking separate clues from what you see, touch, smell, and hear and blending them into one complete picture of your environment.

question: Which imaging tool is considered the gold standard for mapping complex reproductive tract birth defects?

options.A: MRI
options.B: X-ray
options.C: Urinalysis
options.D: Wet mount

explanation: Correct! Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) gives super clear pictures of soft tissues, making it the best choice for planning surgery on complex malformations.

question: In a hospital pharmacy, what does the FEFO inventory rule stand for?

options.A: Free Essential Formulas Only
options.B: Financial Evaluation For Operations
options.C: First-Expired, First-Out
options.D: Fastest Earnings From Outpatients

explanation: Easy and practical! FEFO means you sell the drugs that expire sooner first, so valuable medicine doesn't go to waste on the shelf.

question: What is a core day-to-day duty of nurses and midwives in Nigerian reproductive health care?

options.A: Providing direct clinical care, health education, and community outreach
options.B: Writing national health insurance laws in the federal legislature
options.C: Manufacturing contraceptive implants in national laboratories
options.D: Importing specialized surgical instruments from overseas

explanation: Exactly! Nurses and midwives are on the frontline, delivering care at the bedside and educating communities on healthy living.

question: A patient is terrified to tell their spouse about their HIV diagnosis. What is a helpful nursing action?

options.A: Contact the spouse immediately without telling the patient
options.B: Tell the patient that spouses never react with anger
options.C: Offer to help prepare for the conversation through role-play
options.D: Advise the patient to keep the diagnosis a secret forever

explanation: You got this! Role-playing and talking through the steps helps build the patient's confidence to share their status safely.

question: A patient has high levels of a hormone in their blood, yet shows symptoms of a deficiency. What is going on?

options.A: Excessive clearance of hormones by the liver
options.B: Target cell receptor resistance or signal defect
options.C: An increase in total receptor number on cells
options.D: Complete destruction of the endocrine gland

explanation: This is a classic sign of hormone resistance! There's plenty of the hormone around, but the cells' receptors aren't responding to it, leading to deficiency symptoms anyway.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical focus of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) for sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Reframing unhelpful beliefs regarding sexuality
options.B: Reducing anxiety related to sexual performance
options.C: Surgical reconstruction of the pelvic floor muscles
options.D: Challenging negative thoughts about body image

explanation: Spot on! CBT is all about thoughts, feelings, and behaviors—surgeries are definitely left for surgical specialists!

question: What procurement practice helps health authorities buy essential medicines at a much lower cost?

options.A: Bulk purchasing using generic non-proprietary names
options.B: Ordering exclusively through expensive luxury suppliers
options.C: Importing only patented brand-name formulations
options.D: Buying small batches from local retail pharmacies daily

explanation: Great job! Buying large quantities of generics lets health systems take advantage of bulk discounts.

question: Why is swelling of the kidney (hydronephrosis) during pregnancy more common on the right side?

options.A: Progesterone affects the right ureter muscle fibers exclusively
options.B: The pregnant uterus typically displaces toward the right side
options.C: The right renal artery has higher blood pressure
options.D: The right kidney is anatomically larger than the left kidney

explanation: Think of the growing womb leaning slightly to the right side of the pelvis, placing direct mechanical pressure on the right tube carrying urine away from the kidney.

question: What is one effective strategy to ensure two-way communication in a referral system?

options.A: Banning clients from ever returning to their original health post
options.B: Using standardized feedback forms sent back by the receiving facility
options.C: Destroying all medical records once a client leaves the primary clinic
options.D: Stopping all phone calls between hospitals and primary centers

explanation: Two-way feedback forms allow receiving hospitals to report back to the referring nurse on the client's outcome. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h8)

question: Which of the following will NOT typically cause prevalence to increase?

options.A: An increase in new infections
options.B: A long duration of the illness
options.C: Migration of sick people into the town
options.D: A high death rate from the disease

explanation: A high mortality rate removes people from the population quickly, which lowers prevalence rather than raising it. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h4)

question: What kind of data do we usually analyze using a Chi-Square test?

options.A: Ratio level measurements
options.B: Paired interval scores
options.C: Continuous numerical data
options.D: Categorical data

explanation: You've got this! A Chi-Square test is used for data that falls into distinct groups or categories (like male/female or yes/no), rather than numbers on a continuous scale.

question: Which nursing intervention is essential for managing patients with hormone imbalances affecting fluid and electrolytes?

options.A: Tracking fluid intake and output records accurately
options.B: Restricting all forms of physical movement in bed
options.C: Applying warm compresses to the thyroid gland daily
options.D: Checking visual acuity every two hours around the clock

explanation: Monitoring fluid balance helps nurses catch early signs of dangerous electrolyte shifts and kidney stress caused by hormonal changes. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T7#GNS211_U1_T7_h6)

question: A postoperative patient asks to have her temperature taken rectally. What is the correct nursing response?

options.A: Refuse to check her temperature at all during the entire hospital stay
options.B: Perform the rectal temperature quickly and gently with lots of lubrication
options.C: Ask the patient to insert the thermometer herself to avoid causing pain
options.D: Explain that rectal temperatures are contraindicated to protect the surgical repair

explanation: Any instrument placed in the rectum can damage the fresh surgical repair site and cause the surgery to fail. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h8)

question: Which cells in the pancreas are responsible for producing insulin?

options.A: Alpha cells
options.B: Beta cells
options.C: Delta cells
options.D: Acinar cells

explanation: Insulin is synthesized and secreted by the beta cells located within the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T17#GNS324_U4_T17_h1)

question: During a vaginal exam, a student midwife feels the baby's skull bones overlapping tightly with no way to separate them. How is this charted?

options.A: Grade 2 or Grade 3 moulding
options.B: Normal physiological shift
options.C: Caput succedaneum score
options.D: Grade 0 normal molding

explanation: When bones overlap firmly and won't budge, that's advanced moulding (Grade 2 or 3). It's a key sign to watch out for to prevent prolonged or blocked labour!

question: A patient asks why the doctor adjusts their tiopronin dose using 24-hour urine collections. What is your best nursing response?

options.A: To find the exact dose that lowers your urine cystine enough to stop stones from forming
options.B: To check if your liver is completely immune to protein toxicity
options.C: To measure how much calcium your bones are losing while taking the drug
options.D: To ensure you are drinking the exact recommended liters of soda daily

explanation: We use 24-hour urine tests to find the sweet spot: enough medicine to keep cystine levels low and prevent stones, without taking more than necessary.

question: How has the traditional Almajiri system in some parts of Nigeria unfortunately contributed to street children numbers?

options.A: Extreme poverty has stripped away structural support, leaving pupils to beg for survival
options.B: Religious teachers train children specifically to migrate to foreign countries
options.C: The government mandates that all Quranic students live exclusively outdoors
options.D: Boarding facilities for students are overfunded and turn children away

explanation: You're doing great. When the system lacks enough food and shelter resources, young students are left with no choice but to beg on the streets to eat.

question: Which of the following is considered a classic sign of maternal depletion that a nurse should watch out for?

options.A: Chronic fatigue and hair loss
options.B: Rapid thickening of tooth enamel
options.C: Decreased need for hours of sleep
options.D: Sudden increase in physical stamina

explanation: When a mother's nutritional stores run low to support milk production, she may experience exhaustion, hair thinning, and fatigue. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h8)

question: Which of these tasks is NOT part of a nurse's daily responsibilities when dealing with LFTs?

options.A: Monitoring the blood draw site for bleeding afterward
options.B: Diagnosing the specific stage of cirrhosis from the lab slip
options.C: Ensuring proper patient preparation and fasting if required
options.D: Checking patient medication history for drugs that stress the liver

explanation: That's right! We prep the patient, check medications, and keep them safe, but making the final disease diagnosis is the doctor's job.

question: During discharge planning, which hospital professional do nurses commonly work with to help a patient's financial needs?

options.A: Hospital maintenance engineers
options.B: Medical social workers
options.C: Pharmaceutical sales reps
options.D: IT staff

explanation: Medical social workers are our best friends when it comes to connecting patients with welfare, charity funds, and community support!

question: What big problem happens if irrigation fluid keeps flowing into the bladder but refuses to drain out?

options.A: Sudden and permanent kidney failure
options.B: Extreme drop in body temperature
options.C: Bladder over-distension and severe pain
options.D: Severe swelling of the lower feet

explanation: If fluid gets trapped, the bladder walls stretch way too much, leading to major pain and potential tissue damage.

question: What is the primary action of vasopressor medications like norepinephrine in shock?

options.A: Dissolve blood clots in the coronary arteries
options.B: Dilate the bronchial tubes in the lungs
options.C: Slow down a rapid heart rate
options.D: Constrict blood vessels to raise blood pressure

explanation: Vasopressors cause blood vessels to tighten, which increases vascular resistance and helps raise blood pressure when fluids are not enough. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h6)

question: What is the term for the uterus shrinking back down to its normal size after birth?

options.A: Fundal subinvolution
options.B: Uterine involution
options.C: Endometrial hyperplasia
options.D: Myometrial contraction

explanation: Think of 'involution' as the uterus gracefully rolling back down to its pre-pregnancy size. Great midwifery term to know!

question: A patient with severe malaria isn't getting better despite finishing a full course of drugs bought from an unverified roadside vendor. What should you suspect?

options.A: The patient requires an immediate surgical intervention for appendicitis.
options.B: The hospital ward is experiencing an outbreak of a normal bacterial infection.
options.C: The patient's body has suddenly developed a lifelong immunity to all fevers.
options.D: The medication administered may be substandard or counterfeit.

explanation: When a trusted drug completely fails to work—especially from a shady source—always suspect that it might be a fake or low-quality product.

question: How does losing estrogen generally affect a woman's heart health?

options.A: It prevents the formation of atherosclerotic plaques
options.B: It permanently lowers blood pressure and heart rate
options.C: It increases high-density lipoprotein levels significantly
options.D: It leads to unfavorable changes in cholesterol levels and blood vessels

explanation: Estrogen helps keep blood vessels flexible and cholesterol balanced, so losing it can increase heart disease risks over time.

question: A patient asks why her body doesn't reject the developing pregnancy as a foreign object. What is the best way to explain this?

options.A: The baby carries the exact same blood type as the mother always
options.B: The placenta completely blocks all maternal blood cells from forming
options.C: The mother's immune system shuts down completely during pregnancy
options.D: The outer trophoblast layer actively modifies local immune responses

explanation: The placenta and outer cells are clever—they whisper to the immune system to stay calm so the baby can grow safely. Clinical communication made simple!

question: Why does a nurse monitor the activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) for a patient receiving heparin?

options.A: To measure the exact number of active platelets in the bloodstream
options.B: To check if the patient has developed an iron deficiency anemia
options.C: To ensure the intrinsic and common pathways are appropriately suppressed
options.D: To evaluate how well the liver is producing new red blood cells

explanation: Heparin affects the intrinsic pathway, so checking the aPTT lets the nurse know if the drug dose is safe and effective. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h7)

question: A public health team rushes to a village to investigate a sudden outbreak of measles only. What type of assessment are they doing?

options.A: Problem-oriented community diagnosis
options.B: National census data collection
options.C: Hospital morbidity survey
options.D: Comprehensive community diagnosis

explanation: You're getting the hang of it! When we zero in on one specific issue or outbreak instead of looking at the whole community, we call it a problem-oriented approach.

question: What is the main goal of the fluid released by the bulbourethral glands?

options.A: To stimulate testosterone production
options.B: To form the hard outer shell of semen
options.C: To provide primary nutrition for sperm
options.D: To neutralize acid in the urethra

explanation: Since urine is acidic and passes through the same tube, the bulbourethral glands send out a clear mucus to clean and neutralize the path right before ejaculation.

question: What is a common everyday habit that shows bias against people with physical disabilities?

options.A: Mandatory medical quarantine during routine community gatherings
options.B: Strict government laws requiring daily public registration
options.C: Speaking to an accompanying person instead of addressing the individual directly
options.D: Automatic exemption from paying all forms of local utility taxes

explanation: Spot on! Talking to their friend or family member instead of the patient assumes their disability affects their mind, which is a common bias we need to unlearn.

question: What makes teenagers feel comfortable enough to seek out reproductive health services?

options.A: Public waiting rooms with adult family members present
options.B: Requiring parental permission for every simple checkup
options.C: Mandatory reporting of all visits to school authorities
options.D: Assured confidentiality and a non-judgmental environment

explanation: Teens want to know their secrets are safe. When they trust their privacy is respected, they are much more likely to seek proper healthcare.

question: Why is it helpful to properly prepare a client before she visits the family planning clinic?

options.A: It prevents the clinic staff from asking her any personal questions
options.B: It reduces anxiety and increases the likelihood she will attend
options.C: It eliminates the need for any further medical history taking
options.D: It guarantees that she will receive free services at the facility

explanation: When clients know what to expect and where to go, they feel much more confident and are way more likely to show up!

question: What is the main goal of civil service rules for government workers?

options.A: To replace the professional nursing curriculum set by the council
options.B: To provide a standard framework for employment and administrative conduct
options.C: To dictate the specific clinical medications nurses can prescribe
options.D: To determine the personal income tax rates for civil servants

question: What is the safest sleeping position to teach parents to prevent SIDS (cot death)?

question: What best describes a near-miss in a clinical environment?

question: What is the main root cause of inherited degenerative diseases that affect the brain?

question: What is the normal adult reference range for white blood cells?

question: What is 'moral distress' in nursing?

question: A pregnant patient complains of severe lower back ache after standing for hours at her market stall. What is the main cause?

question: Why is training in adolescent psychology helpful for clinical nurses?

question: What is the main use of a partograph during labor?

question: Why do daily wage earners find it difficult to attend primary healthcare clinics during the day?

question: Why do endocrine problems usually cause a full-body crisis instead of just a local issue?

question: Why should nurses take time to understand a patient's cultural or identity group?

question: Why should a nurse check local market days and religious schedules before setting a date for a community health talk?

question: What causes the noisy breathing sound often called the death rattle in a dying patient?

options.C: It has no effect on skeletal development or bone length
options.D: It accelerates bone growth but also causes early closure of growth plates

explanation: You nailed it! Estrogen gives teens a fast growth spurt at first, but it also signals the growth plates to eventually fuse and close up.

question: Why do some patients with gallbladder disease develop jaundice (yellow skin)?

options.A: Bilirubin backs up into the bloodstream because a bile duct is blocked
options.B: Fatty foods destroy the skin's surface pigments
options.C: The liver stops producing red blood cells
options.D: Stomach acid leaks through the gallbladder wall

explanation: You nailed it! When a stone blocks the bile duct, bilirubin cannot flow to the intestines, so it builds up in the blood and turns the skin yellow.

question: How does home-school communication improve child health outcomes?

options.A: It stops children from visiting hospitals when they are ill
options.B: It allows parents to grade the health teachers directly
options.C: It removes the need for any formal classroom teaching
options.D: It ensures health habits taught at school are practiced at home

explanation: Consistency between home teachings and school lessons helps children adopt and maintain proper hygiene and health practices. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h4)

question: What can happen if a breastfeeding mother drastically cuts her calories to lose weight too fast?

options.A: It stops the infant from sleeping
options.B: It can reduce the daily milk supply
options.C: It causes permanent bone density loss
options.D: It changes the baby's blood type

explanation: Crash dieting sends a signal to the body to slow down and conserve energy, which can unfortunately cause your milk supply to drop. Slow and steady wins the race!

question: Why are serial weight measurements over several months more useful than a single isolated measurement in children?

options.A: They show the actual growth velocity and long-term nutritional trend
options.B: They correct for any errors made by the scale manufacturer
options.C: They eliminate the need to measure the child's height
options.D: They prevent the child from moving around during the visit

explanation: Growth is a dynamic process, and plotting multiple weights on a growth chart reveals whether a child is developing normally over time. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h6)

question: Which type of medication is prescribed to clear up oral candidiasis (thrush)?

options.A: Antihistamines
options.B: Antifungals
options.C: Antivirals
options.D: Antibiotics

explanation: Since thrush is a fungal infection, antifungal drugs like nystatin are just what the doctor ordered!

question: What is the main goal when doing rehabilitation care for older adults?

options.A: Accelerating the normal aging process in the body
options.B: Curing all chronic illnesses present in the patient
options.C: Maximizing the patient's independence and function
options.D: Providing permanent custodial nursing home placement

explanation: You're doing great! Gerontological rehab is all about helping older adults do as much as they can for themselves, rather than just chasing a cure for old age. Keep it up!

question: Why is self-care considered vital for professional nurses rather than being a selfish act?

options.A: Hospital accreditation standards legally penalize nurses who do not take vacations
options.B: Nurses must protect their own well-being to sustain safe, compassionate patient care
options.C: Personal hobbies prevent nurses from ever feeling sad about patient deaths
options.D: Self-care completely eliminates the physical risks of shift work

explanation: You nailed it! Remember: you cannot pour from an empty cup. Taking care of yourself is a core part of being a great nurse.

question: Why is it important for a nurse researcher to know about different scales of measurement?

options.A: To calculate the exact financial cost of a hospital ward
options.B: To determine which nurses get promoted to head nurse
options.C: To bypass the hospital ethics committee approval process
options.D: To select the correct statistical tests for data analysis

explanation: Different types of data need different mathematical tools. Knowing your measurement scale helps you pick the right statistical test to make sense of your findings.

question: Which muscle site is generally considered the safest and most reliable for giving an intramuscular injection to an adult?

options.A: Ventrogluteal
options.B: Rectus femoris
options.C: Dorsogluteal
options.D: Deltoid

explanation: Brilliant! The ventrogluteal site is clear of major nerves and big blood vessels, making it a nurse's best friend for adult IM shots.

question: What is the most crucial instruction for a patient who has just used an epinephrine auto-injector?

options.A: Take a hot shower to wash off any remaining allergen
options.B: Seek immediate emergency medical help at a hospital
options.C: Eat a small meal to restore normal blood sugar levels
options.D: Go to sleep quietly to let the medication take full effect

explanation: Epinephrine buys precious time, but it wears off. Every patient who uses an auto-injector must head straight to the hospital for monitoring.

question: Which heart condition is strongly linked to long-term chronic insomnia?

options.A: Hypertension
options.B: Pulmonary valve stenosis
options.C: Infective endocarditis
options.D: Congenital heart defect

explanation: When your body stays in a constant state of hyperarousal and misses out on restorative rest, your resting blood pressure creeps up, raising your risk for hypertension.

question: Which sign is a classic clue of right-sided heart congestion?

options.A: Complete loss of vision in both eyes
options.B: Sudden wheezing and frothy pink sputum
options.C: Severe sharp chest pain radiating to the jaw
options.D: Peripheral edema and jugular venous distension

explanation: When the right side backs up, blood dams up in the body's veins. This leads to swollen ankles (edema) and bulging neck veins (jugular venous distension).

question: What is an important duty of a community health nurse when dealing with voluntary agencies?

options.A: Referring vulnerable patients to appropriate agency programs
options.B: Managing the global headquarters of faith-based charities
options.C: Auditing the financial tax accounts of all international donors
options.D: Passing new national legislation for non-profit groups

explanation: Correct! As a nurse, knowing what local agencies offer helps you connect your patients to free or low-cost support outside the hospital.

question: Why should community health nurses team up with traditional birth attendants and local leaders?

options.A: To collect financial taxes from rural households
options.B: To stop all traditional practices permanently by force
options.C: To ensure coordinated care and prompt referral of dangerous cases
options.D: To hand over all clinical nursing duties to local leaders

explanation: Working hand-in-hand with local leaders builds strong community trust, ensuring that mothers with complications get rushed to the hospital safely and quickly.

question: What is the primary difference between an arranged marriage and a forced marriage?

options.A: The involvement of religious leaders
options.B: The age of the individuals getting married
options.C: The right to refuse and give full consent
options.D: The geographic location of the ceremony

explanation: In an arranged marriage, the individuals still have the freedom to say no, whereas a forced marriage happens without their consent. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T10#GNS312_U1_T10_h1)

question: What term describes the gradual age-related decline of immune system function in elderly adults?

options.A: Immunosenescence
options.B: Immunoglobulin deficiency
options.C: Hypersensitivity reaction
options.D: Autoimmune suppression

explanation: Immunosenescence refers to the natural weakening of the immune system that happens as people grow older. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h6)

question: Why do nurses love using line diagrams instead of long tables of numbers to track trends?

options.A: They completely eliminate the need to collect raw numerical data.
options.B: They are the only graphic allowed in international nursing journals.
options.C: They prevent any mathematical errors from happening during data entry.
options.D: They make it much easier to spot upward or downward movement at a single glance.

explanation: Exactly! Pictures speak louder than numbers. A quick look at a line lets your brain grasp the whole story instantly.

question: Why are regular debriefing sessions important for palliative care nurses?

options.A: They replace the need for personal time off and vacation days
options.B: They are required by hospital administrators to track daily task completion
options.C: They punish nurses who make clinical errors during patient shifts
options.D: They provide a safe space to process difficult emotional experiences with peers

explanation: Debriefing allows nurses to share their heavy experiences, reduce stress, and prevent burnout through collective support. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h8)

question: What practical method do community health nurses use while moving through a neighborhood to observe living conditions?

options.A: Surgical audit
options.B: Windshield survey
options.C: Biopsy screening
options.D: Laboratory blood analysis

explanation: Correct! A windshield survey is an observational method where the nurse travels through a community to spot living conditions and local resources. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T18#GNS225_U5_T18_h4)

question: How does provider bias negatively affect women seeking post-abortion care?

options.A: It automatically lowers the cost of prescription antibiotics and painkillers
options.B: It causes delays in treatment, poor quality care, and discourages women from seeking help
options.C: It improves the speed at which emergency surgical instruments are sterilized
options.D: It guarantees that the patient receives specialized psychological therapy

explanation: Spot on. When health workers show judgmental attitudes, patients hide information or avoid health facilities, making things worse.

question: Which print material is best to hang on a busy clinic waiting room wall to grab quick attention?

options.A: Posters
options.B: Textbooks
options.C: Logbooks
options.D: Brochures

explanation: Posters are large and eye-catching, making them perfect for high-traffic walls where patients can quickly glance at them while waiting.

question: Why are oral medication doses often higher than intravenous doses of the same drug?

options.A: Oral medications dissolve much slower in the bloodstream than IV fluids
options.B: The stomach acid completely destroys most active drug ingredients
options.C: Part of the drug is broken down by the liver before reaching the bloodstream
options.D: The intestines absorb only a tiny fraction of swallowed medicines

explanation: The first-pass effect breaks down a portion of the oral drug in the liver, meaning a higher dose is needed to achieve the same therapeutic effect as an IV dose. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h1)

question: What makes tonsil sponges different from standard gauze swabs?

options.A: They do not need to be counted during surgical operations
options.B: They are made entirely of synthetic plastic fibers
options.C: They are small and attached to strings for throat procedures
options.D: They are soaked in antibiotics before entering the theater

explanation: Because throat procedures are narrow, tonsil sponges come with attached strings so they can't accidentally slip down the airway!

question: Why is it important to ask if a patient has ever had surgery on their neck?

options.A: It can damage the thyroid or parathyroid glands
options.B: It stops the pancreas from producing insulin
options.C: It leads to chronic respiratory infections
options.D: It always causes permanent high blood pressure

explanation: Spot on! Because the thyroid and parathyroid glands live right in the neck, past surgeries there can sometimes accidentally disrupt hormone control.

question: An exposed person stays completely healthy past the maximum known incubation period for that bug. What can you safely conclude as a nurse?

options.A: The person is now immune for the rest of their life
options.B: The pathogen has entered a permanent latent stage
options.C: The person did not contract the infection from the exposure
options.D: The quarantine period must be doubled just to be safe

explanation: Correct! If no symptoms show up within the maximum window, it means they dodged the infection.

question: Which of the following is considered a direct source of data for maternal mortality?

options.A: General household census questionnaires
options.B: Retrospective community interviews about sisters
options.C: Hospital admission and delivery registers
options.D: Mathematical models based on neighboring countries

explanation: Hospital registers and civil registration records capture actual events directly as they are documented in health facilities or official registries. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T016#GNS226_U1_T016_h3)

question: Which specific detail about a suspected drug is critical to include on an ADR form so regulators can trace the manufacturing lot?

options.A: Shipping company
options.B: Factory location
options.C: Batch number
options.D: Advertising agency

explanation: The batch number lets regulators check if a bad reaction is happening because of a flaw in one specific manufacturing batch of the medicine.

question: A patient asks why taking gym steroids can cause infertility. How should you explain it?

options.A: Testosterone supplements cause the blood-testis barrier to permanently close off blood supply
options.B: External hormones trick the brain into stopping natural LH and FSH production, which shuts down sperm creation in the testes
options.C: High hormone levels cause the prostate gland to block the urethra completely
options.D: Anabolic steroids directly dissolve mature sperm stored inside the epididymis and vas deferens

explanation: When you put artificial testosterone into the body, the brain thinks, 'We have too much!' and stops making the hormones (LH and FSH) that tell the testes to make sperm.

question: A patient's adult children demand you stop pain meds because of fear of addiction, but the alert patient wants relief. Whose wish wins?

options.A: The adult children because they pay the household bills
options.B: The family doctor without asking the patient again
options.C: The patient because autonomy gives competent individuals the right to choose
options.D: Hospital policy regarding family involvement

explanation: Exactly! Family care is wonderful, but a mentally competent patient's personal choice (autonomy) always comes first.

question: If you find a patient's PMI shifted far to the left, what does that usually suggest?

options.A: Collapse of the right lung
options.B: Normal athletic heart conditioning
options.C: Dehydration and low blood volume
options.D: Enlargement of the heart

explanation: When the heart muscle gets bigger or stretched out, the PMI moves downward and outward to the left. Spotting this helps you catch complications early! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h7)

question: In Social Cognitive Theory, what do we mean by 'self-efficacy'?

options.A: A doctor's skill in diagnosing lifestyle diseases
options.B: The rate at which a community accepts new public health laws
options.C: A person's belief in their ability to succeed in performing a specific task
options.D: The financial cost required to maintain a healthy diet

explanation: Well done! Self-efficacy is simply your confidence in your own ability to pull off a specific action or goal.

question: Why is it important to dim the lights in the examination room before starting?

options.A: Darkness prevents the patient from blinking too many times
options.B: Dim lighting causes the patient's pupils to dilate naturally
options.C: Low light calms down patients who have severe anxiety
options.D: Bright light causes the ophthalmoscope bulb to burn out quickly

explanation: Reducing ambient room light causes natural pupillary dilation, which gives the examiner a wider opening to look through. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why is it helpful to involve community members when prioritizing health problems?

options.A: It guarantees that no one will ever fall sick in the community again
options.B: It prevents the government from spending any money on the project
options.C: It removes the need for the nurse to write a formal health report
options.D: It ensures the chosen priority matches what the people care about most

explanation: When the community helps choose what to fix first, they feel respected and are much more willing to support the health project.

question: What is the main focus of end-of-life care when a patient is being cared for at home?

options.A: Complete reversal of chronic terminal diseases
options.B: Strict physical rehabilitation exercises
options.C: Aggressive curative surgeries and treatments
options.D: Comfort, pain control, and symptom management

explanation: Great job! At the end of life, the priority shifts completely from chasing cures to making sure the patient is free of pain and as comfortable as possible.

question: The sagittal suture connects which two bones of the foetal skull?

options.A: The frontal and parietal bones
options.B: The two parietal bones
options.C: The temporal and frontal bones
options.D: The parietal and occipital bones

explanation: Think of the sagittal suture as the line running right down the middle of the top of the head, joining the left and right parietal bones together!

question: You want to find out what a patient ate over the past 24 hours. Which assessment tool should you use?

options.A: A physical skin examination
options.B: An anthropometric weighing
options.C: A 24-hour food recall
options.D: A biochemical blood draw

question: What makes chlorhexidine gluconate a popular antiseptic choice in the theatre?

options.A: It works instantly with zero contact time
options.B: It kills viruses faster than any other chemical
options.C: It is easily washed away by hard water
options.D: It keeps fighting bacteria and prevents growth for hours

explanation: Chlorhexidine is great because it binds to your skin and keeps working long after you've finished scrubbing!

question: What is the best way to handle a patient who is extremely anxious about minor symptoms?

options.A: Scold them for wasting valuable hospital time
options.B: Discharge them immediately from the clinic ward
options.C: Validate their feelings and offer gentle reassurance
options.D: Ignore their complaints until lab results come out

explanation: Never dismiss their fear! Validating their emotions builds instant trust and helps them calm down.

question: After a safe delivery, which eye ointment do you apply right away to protect a newborn from eye infections?

options.A: Atropine sulfate drops
options.B: Chloramphenicol eye drops
options.C: Hydrocortisone eye gel
options.D: Tetracycline eye ointment

explanation: Brilliant! Tetracycline 1% eye ointment is standard care to shield baby's eyes from harmful bacteria passed during birth.

question: What happens to a DRF if hospital staff constantly collect drugs on credit and fail to pay back?

options.A: The suppliers will double the credit period for future orders
options.B: The pharmacy will automatically start generating higher profits
options.C: The fund will quickly experience cash depletion and stockouts
options.D: The government will automatically inject fresh emergency funds

explanation: Unpaid credit creates holes in the system. If the cash doesn't come back in, the pharmacy won't have money to buy new medicines when patients need them.

question: A child is rushed to the ward with severe, complicated malaria. What is the best first step regarding their medications?

options.A: Refuse treatment until the family pays cash for the full prescription
options.B: Wait for hospital accountants to review the family's bank statements
options.C: Send the parents out to buy drugs from a commercial chemist across the street
options.D: Provide necessary emergency anti-malarials immediately under the exemption policy

question: Your patient just took a sip of water and now sounds wet and gurgling when they speak. What is your very first nursing move?

options.A: Document normal finding and continue the meal
options.B: Stop feeding immediately and assess the airway
options.C: Encourage the patient to talk more to clear the voice
options.D: Offer a thicker fluid to clear the throat

question: What is the main job of your nasal cavity when you breathe in air?

options.A: To store excess air during heavy exercise
options.B: To produce sound waves for vocalization
options.C: To exchange oxygen directly into the bloodstream
options.D: To warm, humidify, and filter incoming air

explanation: Spot on! Your nose acts like a natural air conditioner, warming, cleaning, and moistening the air before it travels down into your lungs.

question: Which statistical test do researchers commonly use to check internal consistency?

options.A: Chi-square test
options.B: Student's t-test
options.C: Pearson correlation
options.D: Cronbach's alpha

explanation: Cronbach's alpha is the go-to statistical number for checking if all the questions in your survey hang together nicely to measure the same thing.

question: What is an important teaching point for patients who use non-nutritive sweeteners?

options.A: Patients must take extra insulin every time they consume stevia or sucralose.
options.B: Artificial sweeteners will cause immediate low blood sugar if taken without food.
options.C: Products labeled sugar-free can still contain carbohydrates and calories from other ingredients.
options.D: Sugar substitutes raise blood glucose faster than natural cane sugar.

question: What is the biggest plus of using a collaborating conflict style?

options.A: It produces a win-win solution that addresses the root cause
options.B: It forces one party to surrender completely
options.C: It avoids face-to-face conversation entirely
options.D: It requires very little time during a busy shift

explanation: It takes time and patience, but collaboration gets to the bottom of the issue so everyone wins.

question: Why is keeping PAC patient information strictly confidential so important?

options.A: A breach of information can lead to severe social stigma or harm
options.B: The Nursing Council requires permanent archiving of all case notes
options.C: It prevents insurance companies from raising premium rates
options.D: Hospital accreditation depends entirely on zero medical errors

explanation: Because abortion carries heavy social stigma around us, a leaked secret can ruin relationships, jobs, or even put a patient's safety at risk.

question: Why is a quiet environment important when conducting a neurological assessment?

options.A: To prevent the hospital equipment from malfunctioning
options.B: To keep the patient fast asleep throughout the examination
options.C: To ensure the lighting remains perfectly dim at all times
options.D: To accurately evaluate mental status, speech, and cranial nerves

explanation: Excessive background noise can distract the patient or mask subtle speech and hearing abnormalities. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h3)

question: A patient's physical body parts and chromosomal makeup are best described as what?

options.A: Gender expression
options.B: Cultural role
options.C: Biological sex
options.D: Social identity

explanation: Chromosomes and physical anatomy define biological sex, which is different from socially learned gender roles. Spot on!

question: What is the main job of haustrations (pocket-like folds) in the colon?

options.A: Adding digestive juices to the food mixture
options.B: Speeding up the travel time of liquid waste
options.C: Pushing stool directly out of the anus
options.D: Mixing food contents to help the body absorb water

explanation: Think of haustrations as gentle churning movements in the large intestine. They mix things up slowly so the bowel lining has enough time to soak up water and minerals!

question: What is the main function of the aggregation stage in the supply chain?

options.A: Setting fixed retail prices for consumers in urban stores
options.B: Gathering small amounts of produce into larger loads for transport
options.C: Testing food items in a laboratory for bacterial contamination
options.D: Processing raw crops into long-lasting canned goods

explanation: Aggregation brings together the harvests of multiple small farmers so they can be economically moved in bulk to city markets. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of monitoring a Behavioural Change Communication program?

options.A: To ensure resources are well-spent and goals are met
options.B: To punish staff members who arrive late to work
options.C: To increase the cost of community health services
options.D: To eliminate the need for future community meetings

explanation: Correct! Monitoring helps nurses track progress, see if the program is working, and make smart adjustments along the way.

question: Which nursing action is an example of primary prevention?

options.A: Teaching joint exercises to a stroke survivor
options.B: Providing wound care for a chronic leg ulcer
options.C: Conducting a blood pressure screening at a market
options.D: Administering the routine childhood measles vaccine

explanation: Vaccines prevent healthy people from developing an infection in the first place, making them a primary prevention measure. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h1)

question: What is a common risk for a woman who uses a secret contraceptive method in a controlling relationship?

options.A: Mandatory enrollment in nursing leadership classes
options.B: Automatic promotion to a higher socioeconomic status
options.C: Instantaneous and permanent relief from all headaches
options.D: Experiencing partner violence or abandonment if found out

explanation: Using birth control without a partner's knowledge in environments with strict gender imbalances can provoke severe domestic conflict and safety risks. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h3)

question: What is a common cultural barrier that stops some communities from accepting routine immunization?

options.A: Strict laws banning children from entering clinics
options.B: The requirement that children must fast before vaccination
options.C: False rumors about vaccine safety and fertility
options.D: A mandatory tax placed on every vaccine dose

explanation: Great thinking! Baseless fears regarding side effects, like fertility issues, are major cultural hurdles we encounter in practice.

question: How full should a waste bag be before you tie it up and remove it from the ward?

options.A: Whenever the shift ends
options.B: Three-quarters full
options.C: Completely packed to the brim
options.D: One-quarter full

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical feature of untreated or severe endometritis?

options.A: Normal spontaneous resolution without any treatment
options.B: Spread of infection into the bloodstream
options.C: Scarring of the inner uterine cavity
options.D: Formation of pus pockets in the pelvis

explanation: Endometritis is serious and won't just go away on its own. Leaving it untreated can lead to nasty complications like abscesses or blood infections.

question: What is the main difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation separates sick people, while quarantine separates exposed healthy people
options.B: Isolation is for bacterial infections, while quarantine is for viral diseases
options.C: Quarantine lasts for one year, while isolation lasts for only two hours
options.D: Quarantine is done in a hospital, while isolation is always done in a market

explanation: Easy way to remember: Isolation is for those who are already sick, while quarantine is for healthy people who were exposed and need to wait out the incubation period.

question: Why is checking 'nutrient density' often better than just counting calories when looking at a patient's diet?

options.A: It measures the amount of vitamins and minerals relative to the calories
options.B: It calculates the exact percentage of body fat a food item will produce
options.C: It determines how fast the digestive system will break down a meal
options.D: It shows the total monetary cost of the food items consumed

explanation: You got it! Nutrient density tells you how many good vitamins and minerals you get per calorie, helping avoid empty calories.

question: What shape does a standard antibody molecule look like?

options.A: Y-shape
options.B: Ring shape
options.C: Flat sheet
options.D: Spiral helix

explanation: Antibodies are shaped like the letter 'Y'. The tips of the Y have variable sites that lock specifically onto matching foreign antigens.

question: How does aseptic technique differ from everyday household cleaning?

options.A: Aseptic technique is only performed by medical doctors
options.B: Aseptic technique aims for the complete absence of disease-producing microbes
options.C: Household cleaning uses stronger bleach solutions than hospitals
options.D: Household cleaning is regulated by strict international health laws

explanation: While cleaning removes visible dirt, aseptic technique specifically targets invisible pathogens to protect patients during vulnerable procedures. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why does the body keep the testes in the scrotum, slightly cooler than the rest of the body?

options.A: To support healthy sperm production
options.B: To maintain normal urinary flow
options.C: To avoid localized skin irritation
options.D: To prevent excessive testosterone breakdown

explanation: Sperm cells are very sensitive! They need a slightly cooler temperature than standard body heat to grow and develop properly.

question: Which of these is NOT a normal sign of recovery after a medical abortion?

options.A: Having light spotting that tapers off over a couple of weeks
options.B: Passing blood clots along with lower abdominal cramping
options.C: A persistent high fever starting several days after misoprostol
options.D: Experiencing mild nausea that goes away within twenty-four hours

question: When you measure a patient's mid-upper arm circumference and body mass index, what kind of assessment are you doing?

options.A: Environmental factors
options.B: Biochemical data
options.C: Clinical signs
options.D: Anthropometric measurements

explanation: Don't let the big word scare you! 'Anthropometric' just means measuring physical body sizes like height, weight, and arm circumference to check nutrition.

question: Why do the kidneys get rid of extra bicarbonate during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: To prevent the mother from developing high blood pressure
options.B: To compensate for severe dehydration caused by morning sickness
options.C: To supply extra nutrients directly to the developing placenta
options.D: To balance out the low carbon dioxide levels and maintain pH

explanation: The kidneys lower bicarbonate to offset the mild alkalosis from deeper breathing, keeping the blood pH right where it needs to be. Well done!

question: What is the main focus of post-abortion care (PAC) services?

options.A: Preventing the client from ever becoming pregnant again
options.B: Filing legal reports against the client in every single case
options.C: Requiring mandatory psychiatric admission for all patients
options.D: Treating incomplete abortion and managing life-threatening complications

explanation: PAC is all about emergency medical care: stopping bleeding, clearing the womb safely, and treating dangerous infections. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h7)

question: Where should a nurse NOT use a local anesthetic mixed with adrenaline?

options.A: On a clean scalp wound
options.B: On a forearm abrasion
options.C: On a large thigh laceration
options.D: On the fingers or toes

explanation: Adrenaline causes blood vessels to constrict tightly, which can cut off blood supply entirely in digits and lead to tissue death. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h2)

question: Roughly what percentage of waste coming out of healthcare facilities is actually considered hazardous?

options.D: 50 to 60 percent

question: Why should nurses discuss advance directives and goals of care early with residents and their families?
